abstract: An Atlanta Fed Workforce Currents brief (DOI 10.29338/wc2026-04) maps demand for AI skills across six southeastern states using Lightcast job postings, 2010–2025. A posting counts as AI-related if it lists at least one skill from a set built from Lightcast's AI/ML and NLP categories plus keyword and manual review. The share of postings requiring AI skills has risen steadily since 2010 and faster in recent years, but stays below the national average in most southeastern states. As of December 2025 Georgia led the region at 2.93% of postings, just under the national 3%. Demand is concentrated in large metros (Atlanta accounts for more than four-fifths of Georgia's AI postings) and spreads little into smaller markets. Most AI postings list only one to four AI skills, which suggests AI is being added to broader roles rather than creating specialist jobs. Demand sits in computer and mathematical, engineering and business operations occupations in every state. Larger metros have more diversified employer bases; smaller markets show higher employer concentration (HHI).
keyFindings: 3% of US job postings required at least one AI skill in December 2025 (national average); Georgia led the Southeast at 2.93%
AI postings are roughly 2%–4% of total job demand within each southeastern state
The Atlanta metro accounts for more than four-fifths of Georgia's AI postings; Florida and Alabama spread AI demand across several metros
Most AI-related postings require only 1–4 AI skills; postings with 10+ AI skills are a small share

AI demand concentrates in computer and mathematical, engineering and business operations occupations; arts/design (3.2%), education (3%), installation/maintenance (3.4%), legal (3.3%) and community/social service (2.1%) each hold 2%–4% of AI demand
Smaller metros (for example Gainesville, Knoxville, Pensacola) show higher employer concentration of AI hiring than large metros
methodology: Lightcast online job postings for Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Louisiana, Mississippi and Tennessee (six-state Sixth District view), 2010–2025. AI-related postings are those with at least one AI skill from a set built from Lightcast Open Skills AI/ML and NLP categories plus keyword search and manual review. County maps restricted to counties with at least 1,000 postings and 500 AI postings. Metrics: AI share of postings, MSA share of statewide AI postings, location quotient against the national share, skill intensity (count of AI skills per posting) and employer concentration (Herfindahl-Hirschman Index).
qualifiers: Tier 2: Federal Reserve staff brief, descriptive and not refereed. Postings measure employer demand for AI skills, not firm adoption, AI use or employment. A one-skill threshold may count roles that only mention AI tools and miss roles that use AI without listing it; the author says results show patterns, not a complete measure of demand. About half of AI postings could not be assigned an occupation code, so occupational shares are rescaled. Regional scope; the only national figure is the 3% benchmark.
